zh.title: 總統府駁回「作秀」說 法稱視導漢光屬責任義務
zh.summary: 總統府發言人郭雅慧表示，總統以三軍統帥身分視導漢光演習屬責任與義務，指稱「作秀」為臆測與扭曲，污名化國軍，強調國家元首參與重大演訓符合國際慣例，且演習採無劇本實戰化，無安排火力秀。
body: 中央社27日報導，有媒體稱總統賴清德在漢光演習期間安排視導是「作秀」。總統府發言人郭雅慧回應，作為三軍統帥，總統在國軍重要演訓期間參與視導，是責任也是義務。
郭雅慧指出，所謂「作秀」之說內容多屬臆測、觀點扭曲，更污名化國軍與國防，令人遺憾。她說，國家元首參與國家重大軍事演訓，無論歐、美、日、韓等國，國際皆然。
自漢光40號演習起，即採取「無劇本、實戰化」演練。總統參與視導，亦由國防部依照演習進程適時規劃，不存在所謂安排「火力秀」的問題。
對於所謂「轉移在野攻擊」、「作秀給選民看」等無端指控，郭雅慧表示，對此刻正為強化國防、守護國家而努力的所有人員極不公平。
總統府重申，總統視導漢光演習屬憲定職權，並非政治作秀，呼籲社會理性看待國防事務。

en.title: Presidential Office rejects “show” claim, says Han Kuang inspection is duty
en.summary: The Presidential Office said President Lai Ching-te’s inspection of the Han Kuang exercise is a constitutional duty of the commander‑in‑chief, dismissing media allegations of a “show” as speculation that defames the military. Spokesperson Guo Ya‑hui noted that heads of state attending major drills is standard practice worldwide, and that since Han Kuang 40 the exercises have been unscripted and realistic, with the President’s visit arranged by the Ministry of National Defense according to the drill schedule. She called accusations of political motives unfair to personnel strengthening national defense.
body: CNA reported on 27 July that some media labelled President Lai Ching-te’s inspection of the Han Kuang exercise a “show”. Presidential Office spokesperson Guo Ya-hui responded that, as commander‑in‑chief, the President’s participation in a major military drill is both a responsibility and an obligation.

Guo said the “show” accusation is largely speculation and a distortion that smears the armed forces and national defence. She added that heads of state attending important military exercises is the norm in Europe, the United States, Japan, South Korea and elsewhere.

Since Han Kuang 40, the drills have been conducted without a script in a realistic manner. The President’s inspection was arranged by the Ministry of National Defense in line with the exercise timeline, and there was no arranged “firepower show”.
Guo dismissed allegations of shifting opposition attacks or staging a performance for voters as baseless and unfair to all personnel working to strengthen defence and protect the country.
The Presidential Office reiterated that the President’s inspection is a constitutional duty, not a political stunt, and urged the public to view defence matters rationally.
